Warm-Up OME355/IDRPT/IV/VIISEM/KG-KiTE After completing this lecture, you will be able to: • Define User Interface (UI) and User Experience (UX). • Explain the differences between UI and UX. • Describe the importance of UI/UX in product development. • Identify common UI components. • Understand the UX design process. • Recognize the role of UI/UX in modern industries.

Introduction • Technology has transformed the way people interact with digital products such as websites, mobile applications, ATMs, smart TVs, wearable devices, and industrial control systems. • Two important concepts that contribute to this goal are User Interface (UI) and UserExperience (UX). UI focuses on the appearance and interactive elements of a product. • UX focuses on the overall experience a user has while interacting with the product. • Together, UI and UX help create products that are visually appealing, easy to learn, efficient to use, and capable of satisfying user needs. Introduction OME355/IDRPT/IV/VIISEM/KG-KiTE • Designing a user interface is not just about creating an attractive screen. A successful interface should match how people think, learn, remember, and interact with technology. • Understanding human psychology helps designers create products that are intuitive, reduce user errors, and improve satisfaction.

Psychology in UI/UX Design Psychology in UI/UX is the study of how users perceive, process, and respond to information while interacting with digital products. It helps answer questions such as: • What attracts users' attention? • Why do users click certain buttons? • How do users make decisions? • What causes confusion or frustration? Human Factors in UI Design Human factors refer to designing products that accommodate users' physical and cognitive abilities. Important Human Factors • Vision (font size, color contrast) • Memory (simple navigation) • Attention (highlight important actions) • Motor skills (button size and spacing) • Accessibility (support for users with disabilities) OME355/IDRPT/IV/VIISEM/KG-KiTE

Cognitive Load • Cognitive load is the amount of mental effort required to use an interface. OME355/IDRPT/IV/VIISEM/KG-KiTE High Cognitive Load Too many buttons Too many colors Complex menus Long forms Technical language Low Cognitive Load Simple layout Clear instructions Logical navigation Minimal options Familiar icons

Gestalt Principles Gestalt principles explain how people naturally organize visual elements. a) Proximity Objects placed close together are perceived as related. b) Similarity Similar colors, shapes, or sizes appear to belong together. c) Continuity The eye follows smooth paths or lines. d) Closure People mentally complete incomplete shapes. e) Figure-Ground Users distinguish foreground objects from the background. Fitts's Law The time to reach a target depends on its size and distance. Implication: Frequently used buttons should be large and easy to reach. Example: Mobile apps place the "Home" button near the bottom for easy thumb access OME355/IDRPT/IV/VIISEM/KG-KiTE
Hick's Law Definition The more choices users have, the longer they take to make a decision. Example Instead of displaying 20 menu options, group them into categories. OME355/IDRPT/IV/VIISEM/KG-KiTE

Miller's Law People can hold about 7 ± 2 items in short-term memory. Application Keep menus concise. Break information into smaller sections. Use progressive disclosure for complex tasks. OME355/IDRPT/IV/VIISEM/KG-KiTE

ABSTRACT The modern Internet of Things (IoT) landscape demands efficient, automated, and lightweight environmental control systems capable of real-time monitoring and responsive actuation. This project presents AeroCool IoT, a full-stack IoT- enabled smart air-cooling system designed to automate temperature control and provide live performance tracking. The system is engineered using a modular architecture comprising a Flask backend, an SQLite database, and an HTML5/CSS3/Vanilla JavaScript frontend rendered via Jinja2, with Chart.js integrated for historical metrics visualization. To achieve continuous operation prior to physical hardware deployment, a dedicated simulation engine simulates realistic, non-random environmental telemetry. The backend incorporates a dynamic control algorithm that automatically calculates fan speed percentages and toggles active cooling states based on pre-configured thermal thresholds (28°C threshold, 35°C critical level). Additionally, an ESP32-ready RESTful endpoint (/api/sensor) is integrated to ensure plug-and-play compatibility with microcontrollers in physical deployments. The result is a highly responsive, lightweight, and modern IoT application capable of automated thermal management and real-time user notification.

CHAPTER 1 INTRODUCTION 1.1 Introduction The Internet of Things (IoT) enables physical systems to be monitored and controlled through connected software applications. Temperature and humidity monitoring is one of the common applications of IoT, where environmental conditions can be continuously observed and used to control cooling systems. The proposed IoT-Enabled Smart Air-Cooling System with Automated Temperature Control and Real-Time Performance Monitoring is a software-based mini project that demonstrates this concept using simulated sensor data. The system generates ambient temperature and relative humidity readings through selectable profiles such as Normal, Warm, Hot, and Cooling Down. The application automatically evaluates the simulated temperature and controls the fan state according to predefined levels such as OFF, LOW, MEDIUM, and HIGH. It also monitors abnormal temperature conditions and generates safety alerts when required. The system provides a web-based dashboard through REST APIs for displaying real-time operational information, KPI summaries and historical temperature data. A persistence layer stores telemetry, operational states, alerts and configuration settings using SQLite. In addition, a Gemini AI service is included to provide operational responses based on the available runtime system data. Since the current project focuses only on the software implementation, physical sensors, ESP32 and cooling hardware are not used.

• To store telemetry and system information for historical analysis. • To provide a real-time web dashboard for system monitoring. • To provide AI-assisted operational responses using runtime system information.

CHAPTER 2 High-Level System Architecture The AeroCool IoT system is designed as a software-based smart air-cooling application using simulated sensor data. The system consists of the following major components: 1. Simulation Engine The Simulation Engine generates continuous ambient temperature (°C) and relative humidity (%) readings. Different operating profiles such as Normal, Warm, Hot, and Cooling Down can be selected to simulate different environmental conditions. 2. Automation Engine The Automation Engine evaluates the current temperature against predefined operating thresholds and determines the appropriate fan state. The system supports different fan levels such as OFF (0%), LOW (30%), MEDIUM (60%), and HIGH (100%). This allows the cooling response to change automatically according to the simulated temperature. 3. Alert Engine The Alert Engine monitors temperature conditions and generates safety alerts when predefined limits are exceeded. It produces HIGH_TEMPERATURE safety events and avoids repeatedly generating the same alert by using deduplication. 4. Persistence Layer The Persistence Layer stores the important system information, including telemetry readings, operational states, alerts and configuration settings. SQLite is used for the current software prototype to provide lightweight local data storage. 5. REST API and Dashboard The REST API provides communication between the backend and the web dashboard. CHAPTER 3 TECHNOLOGY STACK AND IMPLEMENTATION 3.1 Technology Stack The AeroCool IoT system uses a lightweight software stack suitable for a mini project. The major technologies used are: Component Technology Programming Language Python Backend Framework Flask Frontend HTML, CSS, JavaScript Database SQLite API REST API Data Visualization Chart.js AI Service Gemini AI Development Environment Visual Studio Code Table 3.1 : Technology Stack 3.2 Backend Implementation The backend is developed using Python and Flask. Flask manages the application routes, REST API endpoints and communication between the dashboard and database. The backend receives simulated telemetry data from the Simulation Engine and passes it to the Automation and Alert Engines for processing. The processed information is then stored in SQLite and made available to the dashboard through REST APIs.

3.3 Frontend Implementation The user interface is developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The dashboard provides a simple interface for monitoring the current temperature, humidity, fan state, alerts and system performance. It stores: • Telemetry readings • Fan and cooling states • Alerts • System configuration • Other required operational information SQLite is suitable for the mini project because it is lightweight and does not require a separate database server. CHAPTER 7 CONCLUSION AND FUTURE SCOPE 7.1 Conclusion The AeroCool IoT system successfully demonstrates a software-based smart air-cooling solution using simulated temperature and humidity data. The system integrates automated fan control, temperature alerts, data storage, REST APIs and a real-time dashboard. The project provides a simple platform for monitoring system conditions and responding automatically to temperature changes. The Gemini AI service further supports operational monitoring by providing responses based on runtime system data. 7.2 Future Scope The system can be further enhanced by: • Integrating real temperature and humidity sensors. • Connecting an ESP32 or similar IoT device. • Controlling a physical cooling fan. • Adding MQTT-based communication. • Adding energy-consumption monitoring. • Improving the automation algorithm. • Deploying the application on a cloud platform.
